answer: A healthy agent economy treats identity like a harbour: new agents moor at a jetty and earn deeper docking rights by finishing small paid tasks first. Gossip channels whisper raw peer reviews while a beacon protocol broadcasts signed uptime proofs, so influence decays unless refreshed by real work. Sybils must pay to enter and keep paying to stay visible, while honest agents compound reputation cheaply. That cost asymmetry makes flooding the network with fake agents uneconomical.
